subject: Provisional balance smoothing request for May spike
messages:
From: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@orionhealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Orion Health Billing <billing@orionhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected spike in inference usage — provisional smoothing?

Hi Sean,

We noticed a large, unexpected jump in our May usage on the Redwood invoice (invoice #R-2026-05-ORION). The attached export (orion_usage_may.csv) shows a cluster of high-volume calls over a 48-hour window starting 2026-05-11 that we don't recognize. Our procurement team has paused payment pending a quick reconciliation.

Two asks: can Redwood apply a provisional smoothing/credit while we investigate with our infra team, and can you share any immediate visibility into whether that traffic looks like automated test runs or a billing ingestion error on your side? We want to avoid a full stop on the account but also need a short-term remedy.

Happy to hop on a 15-min call — Sara & I will be available this afternoon (PDT).

Thanks,
Sara Mitchell
Head of Cloud Ops
Orion Health
Attachments: orion_usage_may.csv (CSV, 1 file)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected spike in inference usage — provisional smoothing?

Sara — thanks for the heads-up and for sending the CSV. I pulled the usage trace and I see a burst that aligns with an unusually long token window from a single API key that rotated on 2026-05-10.

Short answer: yes, we can apply a provisional smoothing credit while we jointly investigate. Proposed approach:
- Issue a provisional service credit of $12,345 to offset the disputed window (applied as a credit on the June invoice).
- Keep the account active; we will not escalate blocking collections while this is under review.
- Grace and Ben, can you confirm accounting code and whether we need a pre-approved limit or DocuSign approval for credits > $10k?

Sara — I attached a provisional_credit_note_template.pdf for tracking. Two quick asks from your side to help narrow root cause:
1) Confirm whether the API key reported in the CSV was rotated or shared with any internal test harnesses.
2) Provide VAT/tax ID if Orion expects a tax-differentiated credit (EU customers only — not relevant if US).

If you prefer, I can convert the provisional credit to a formal credit note after internal approval; we'll keep you posted.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachments: provisional_credit_note_template.pdf

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Jun 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Unexpected spike in inference usage — provisional smoothing?

Folks — forwarding Orion's spike. Key points: their CSV points at a single API key with a big token window (likely a test harness or misconfigured client). My ask: approve a provisional service credit of $12,345 to be applied to the June invoice and confirm the GL/accounting code.

Rationale: prevents account suspension and buys time for Orion to investigate. If we approve, I will issue a provisional credit note and log as "courtesy adjustment - investigatory" pending final reconciliation.

Preliminary numbers: the disputed window totals ~1.1M tokens. Using their plan's unit price that maps to ~$12.3k. We should cap the provisional at $15k to be safe, but I recommend we provide the exact $12,345 unless Ben indicates we need to round.

Ben — any constraints from finance on issuing credits without a signed SOW amendment or docu sign? Lauren — can you confirm tax/VAT handling and whether this needs to be split if they later claim a taxable reversal?

Thanks,
Sean

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Mitchell <sara.mitchell@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Orion Health Billing <billing@orionhealth.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Credit applied: provisional balance smoothing for May spike (invoice R-2026-05-ORION)

Hi Sara / Orion billing team,

Thanks for the quick call this morning — appreciate the context on the test harness hitting production keys. Per our internal approvals, Redwood has applied a provisional service credit of $12,345.00 to your account; this will appear as a line item on the June invoice (offset code: CRED-INV-2026-06-ORION).

Notes and next steps:
- This is a provisional credit while both teams finish the root-cause review. If the final reconciliation determines that the usage was legitimate, we will discuss re-billing; if not, the provisional credit will be converted to a formal credit note and retained.
- VAT/tax handling: because you are US-based, no VAT split is necessary. If your team provides a VAT ID or indicates non-US billing, please escalate to Lauren for tax reclassification.
- Attachments: I have attached the provisional_credit_note_template.pdf we used for internal tracking; I also uploaded the orion_usage_may.csv that you provided into our billing queue for audit.
- Next milestone: we will reconvene in 10 business days to close the investigation. If Orion's postmortem shows customer-side misconfiguration, we will capture root cause and finalize billing.

If you need the provisional credit documented in a signed form for your procurement, I can initiate a DocuSign agreement referencing the provisional credit (DocuSign:0e3f7a2b).

Thanks again — glad we could avoid a payment hold while we sort this out.

Best regards,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
Attachments: provisional_credit_note_template.pdf, orion_usage_may.csv
